title: Petrel Tool Creation Hierarchy
scope: No-Ocean Petrel MCP and CLI tool design for Petrel 2018.2 automation copy
rule: Use the highest tier that can produce the required outputs with verifiable evidence. Do not move to a lower tier until the higher tier is proven insufficient for the specific task.

required_tool_contract.task: What user-visible Petrel automation task this tool performs.
required_tool_contract.inputs: Named required inputs, including files, project package paths, workflow ids, object selectors, and version assumptions.
required_tool_contract.outputs: Named generated outputs with expected paths, formats, schema, and manifest registration rules.
required_tool_contract.validation: Concrete pass/fail checks, including row counts, checksums, parser checks, Petrel log evidence when applicable, and manifest validation.
required_tool_contract.runtime_boundary: One of zero_gui_python, zero_gui_petrel_workflow_editor, deterministic_gui, or discovery_only.
required_tool_contract.evidence: Report paths, screenshots if GUI is used, before/after snapshots if native workflow storage is changed, and restore reports for probes.

tiers.name: Zero-GUI Python or direct file processing
tiers.description: Read project/export/package files directly with Python or shell tooling, decode what is safely understood, write package outputs, register them, and validate checksums.
use_when: The required data exists in accessible project, export, LAS, CSV, XML, SQLite, JSON, text, or already copied native files.
A Python parser can produce the requested output with enough confidence and traceable evidence.
The task is inventory, metadata extraction, comparison, manifest generation, validation, or safe native-store copying.
tiers.failure_to_next_tier: Only escalate if the requested confirmed Petrel output cannot be decoded from files with enough confidence.

tiers.name: Zero-GUI Petrel Workflow Editor native control
tiers.description: Use existing saved Workflow Editor commands, Petrel command-line workflow execution, workflow variables, or guarded native .ptd parameter edits without desktop GUI interaction.
use_when: A saved Workflow Editor command already exists and can be run through Petrel command-line workflow execution.
A same-length parameter patch is mapped, backed up, exact-offset verified, and restorable.
The native command payload is sufficiently mapped for the requested parameter mutation.
Petrel must author the final universal-format export, but the needed command path already exists in the project.
required_evidence: Petrel workflow log with Status: Workflow run OK when Petrel is launched
native snapshot/compare reports for binary edits
patch and restore reports for probes
tiers.failure_to_next_tier: Escalate only when no saved or safely patchable Workflow Editor command can produce the requested output.

tiers.name: Reusable deterministic GUI workflow
tiers.description: Run a named, declarative GUI micro-workflow with fixed anchors, bounded actions, screenshots, trace logs, and fail-closed output validation.
use_when: Zero-GUI Python cannot decode the requested output.
Zero-GUI Workflow Editor/native control cannot create or run the needed export yet.
The GUI sequence is stable enough to encode as a reusable workflow with inputs, outputs, and postconditions.
The workflow is needed for donor capture, confirmed Petrel export, or temporary production fallback.
tiers.failure_to_next_tier: If a deterministic GUI workflow cannot be made stable, mark the task discovery_only and capture the missing anchors or Petrel-authored donor diff.

tiers.name: Discovery or donor capture only
tiers.description: Use manual or assisted Petrel interaction only to capture evidence, author a donor command, or map native records. Do not present this as an automated tool.
use_when: The GUI path is not stable enough for a deterministic workflow.
A Petrel-authored before/after diff is required before safe native .ptd automation.
The required object references, lengths, indexes, or command envelopes are not mapped.
tiers.failure_to_next_tier: No lower tier exists. The output is a mapping/donor-capture task, not an automation tool.

workflow_composition.description: A tool may be a small workflow of other tools, but each step must keep its tier and evidence boundary explicit.
workflow_composition.composition_rule: A higher-level tool may call lower-level tools only after the decision report records why higher tiers were insufficient for that subtask.
